method: Fresh context, no inherited pixels. Read current frozen bilingual prose and captions, then open the two actual original PNGs and three existing rasters per figure exactly once. No new rasterization, rendering, source edit, geometry edit, or repair.

figures.sourcePixelObservation: One upright fork has two approximately level straight prongs, an open slot and rounded common neck, followed by a short vertical stem and small oval mounting foot joined to one perspective box. Three box faces are visible; the top is mostly blank and the sides are hatched. No hammer, recording apparatus, displacement marks, axes, numeric values, or labels are drawn. The outer rectangle is a print border. The pixels do not establish a top cavity.
figures.editionBoundary: Both frozen prose[2] and caption prose[4] explicitly require a wooden box open at the top. The opening is edition-text-based, not source-pixel-based. The support bridge, English labels, uniform prongs and neutral face shading remain declared modern additions. The hammer and needle described in prose are not silently added to this figure.
figures.nativePreviewObservation: At 640 by 560 the two prongs, open slot, common neck, short stem, oval foot, open-top rim/cavity and small supporting bridge are visible and joined. All three perspective box faces are visible. Tuning fork and Wooden box labels are legible, unclipped and separate from each other. No added axes, measurements, Cyrillic, Chinese lettering, or answer-bearing annotation is visible.

The labels remain readable, but the edition-required open top and source-required mounting structure are not inspectable.

figures.sourcePixelObservation: One continuous thick solid oscillatory trace occupies the middle of one horizontal rectangular frame. It starts on a partial descending stroke and ends on a partial ascending stroke. Counting the actual pixels gives six crests and seven troughs, hence six complete trough-to-trough intervals. Heights and spacing are approximately regular, not given measurements. No axes, ticks, baseline, numbers, units, point labels, dashed curve, arrow, second curve or apparatus is visible.
figures.editionBoundary: Current prose[2] and caption prose[6] identify this as the tuning fork's nearly sinusoidal time trace. The regularized curve and English identifying label are modern additions, not measurements from the source. No numerical period or amplitude is implied.
figures.nativePreviewObservation: At 640 by 320 the frame and connected solid trace are visible. Direct visual counting gives six crests and seven troughs, with partial descending start and ascending end. The curve stays inside the shared frame without additional axes, units or apparatus. Time trace is legible above the curve within the frame.

widthRasterObservations.observation: Only the Time trace label appears on a white background. The entire oscillatory curve and rectangular frame are absent, so neither vibration shape nor extrema can be inspected.
Only the Time trace label appears; the curve and frame remain absent. Readable text alone is not a successful instructional rendering.
